environment.target: Tiger Cloud service (host and credentials redacted)

sales.question: Revenue and units by year: raw hypertable scan vs continuous aggregate

risk.question: Supplier p95 lead time: exact scan of raw samples vs continuous aggregate
risk.note: Aggregate p95 is approximate (uddsketch). If coverage < 100%, the aggregate is materialized-only and misses recent rows until refreshed.

ann.question: pgvector nearest-alias search: latency and recall@5 against an exact scan
ann.note: At this table size the planner may prefer a sequential scan; recall of a forced HNSW scan shows what the index would trade away at scale.

compression.question: How much does native compression shrink each hypertable (compressed chunks only)?

verdict.aggregate_sales: 196x faster warm, identical answers on all 12 years: the case for continuous aggregates.
verdict.risk_all_suppliers: 1.8x faster, p95 within 1.6% of exact: modest win, approximate.
verdict.risk_single_supplier: 1.1x: no meaningful benefit; dominated by the ~29 ms round trip.
verdict.ann: No latency benefit at 459 vectors (planner picks a sequential scan); recall 100% either way. Index matters only at scale.
verdict.compression: 6.7x on bulk_order_lines, 9.9x on fulfillment_samples (compressed chunks only); other hypertables not yet compressed.

limitations: Single connection on a shared managed service; timings vary with load and cache state.
Cold runs may include cache warming by earlier experiments in the same session.
Dataset is largely synthetic or replayed (see docs/DATABASE_ORDER1.md); latency does not depend on that, but no claim about real-world accuracy follows.
